Guide\n\nA small, deterministic HTTP service for D&D 5e helper calculations. It uses only Node.js 26 built-ins (`node:http`, `node:sqlite`, `node:crypto`) and plain JavaScript ES modules.\n\n## Starting and verifying the server\n\n```bash\nPORT=3000 ./run.sh\n```\n\n`run.sh` runs `node server.js` in the foreground. The server binds to `127.0.0.1` and reads the port from the `PORT` environment variable, defaulting to `3000`.\n\nVerify it is up:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health\n# {\"ok\":true}\n```\n\n## Entry point and major files\n\n- **`server.js`** — Entry point. Creates the HTTP server, wires the route table via `lib/router.js`, and starts listening. It calls `db.initDb()` at startup.\n- **`lib/router.js`** — Minimal HTTP router. Routes are registered in order and matched by HTTP method and regex. Captured path segments are spread as positional arguments to the handler.\n- **`lib/db.js`** — Persistence layer. Owns the SQLite `DatabaseSync` connection, the schema, and all CRUD operations. Schema creation is centralized in `ensureSchema()` and used by both initialization and reset. The `TABLE_NAMES` array is kept in dependency order so the reset path can drop child tables before parents.\n- **`lib/domain.js`** — Pure business logic and validation: dice parsing, encounter XP, initiative ordering, ability modifiers, proficiency bonus, auth hashing, and shared validation helpers (`isNonEmptyString`, `isPositiveInteger`, `isValidSlug`, etc.). Shared constants such as `ABILITY_NAMES` live here.\n- **`lib/http.js`** — Shared HTTP utilities: body reading, JSON responses, and common error helpers (`badRequest`, `unauthorized`, `notFound`, `methodNotAllowed`, `conflict`).\n- **`lib/handlers.js`** — HTTP request handlers, organized by domain (health, storage, auth, dice, checks, characters, PHB rules, combat, compendium, campaigns, and DM helpers). Combat handlers share small private helpers (`activeCombatant`, `publicOrder`, `publicCondition`, `publicConditions`) to keep response formatting consistent.\n- **`run.sh`** — Foreground startup script.\n\n## State, persistence, and routing\n\n### Persistence\n\n- SQLite database file: `game.db` in the project root.\n- Schema version is fixed at `1` and exposed via `/v1/storage/status`.\n- Tables: `users`, `combat_sessions`, `monsters`, `items`, `campaigns`, `characters`, `events`, `factions`, `npcs`, `quests`, `campaign_inventory`, `character_equipment`, `crafting_projects`, `campaign_sessions`, `session_attendance`, `play_campaigns`, `play_members`, `play_narrations`.\n- JSON arrays/objects (initiative order, combat conditions, monster tags) are serialized to `TEXT` columns with `JSON.stringify`/`JSON.parse`.\n- `/v1/storage/reset` drops all tables and recreates them. This is the only destructive endpoint and is intended for tests. The drop order follows the dependency order in `lib/db.js` so foreign-key constraints are satisfied.\n\n### Request routing\n\n`server.js` builds a `Router` from `lib/router.js`. Routes are evaluated in registration order, and the first matching method/pattern wins. Parameterized routes are placed before more general parents so they are not accidentally shadowed.\n\nThe router preserves the following behavior, which the cumulative evaluator suite depends on:\n\n- `GET` without a matching route returns `405 Method Not Allowed` and does not read the body.\n- `POST` without a matching route reads the body, then returns `404 Not Found`.\n- Any other HTTP method returns `405 Method Not Allowed` without reading the body.\n\n`POST` handlers receive the raw body on `req.body` as a string. Handlers parse it with `lib/http.js::parseJson` via `lib/handlers.js::requireBody`. Invalid JSON returns `400 invalid json`.\n\n## Main API / domain groupings\n\n| Group | Endpoints | Purpose |\n|-------|-----------|---------|\n| **Health** | `GET /health` | Liveness check. |\n| **Keep handlers thin**: handlers validate input, call `lib/db.js` or `lib/domain.js`, and format responses. Business rules belong in `lib/domain.js`.\n- **Add routes in order**: new routes go into the `createRouter()` chain in `server.js` in the order they should be checked. Place parameterized routes before general ones that could shadow them.\n- **Use the shared validation helpers**: prefer `domain.isNonEmptyString`, `domain.isPositiveInteger`, `domain.isNonNegativeInteger`, `domain.isValidSlug`, `domain.isStringArray`, and `domain.ABILITY_NAMES` for consistent error messages and shapes.\n- **Preserve response shapes and status codes**: existing endpoints have fixed response bodies required by the cumulative test suite. Any changes must keep status codes and JSON keys identical.\n- **Centralize schema changes**: when adding or changing tables, update `lib/db.js` only. Keep `TABLE_NAMES` in dependency order so `resetDb()` remains safe.\n- **JSON bodies**: all handlers use `requireBody` from `lib/handlers.js`, which wraps `lib/http.js::parseJson`. Invalid JSON returns `400 invalid json`.\n- **Errors**: `badRequest` → `400 { error }`, `unauthorized` → `401 { error }`, `notFound` → `404 { error: 'not found' }`, `methodNotAllowed` → `405 { error: 'method not allowed' }`, `conflict` → `409 { error }`. Uncaught errors log to stderr and return `500 { error: 'internal server error' }`.\n- **No external dependencies**: do not add npm packages or TypeScript. The project uses only Node.js stdlib modules and plain `.js` ES modules (`\"type\": \"module\"` in `package.json`).\n- **Determinism**: avoid randomness in business logic. The only randomness is `crypto.randomBytes` when generating password salts.\n- **Combat condition formatting**: when exposing conditions in responses, use the shared `publicCondition` /
